findings.text: W losowanym badaniu krzyżowym każda sesja trwała około 4 godzin przed snem przez pięć wieczorów.
findings.why: The only stored source for this study is an abstract (Europe PMC). The abstract gives no design details: no randomisation, no 4-hour exposure, no five evenings. The upstream span gives crossover, about 4 hours and 5 nights, which is a lead, not evidence. The word losowanym (randomised) is in neither text. The item states these design details as established, so the evidence statement is stronger than the checked source. The same missing exposure details (about 4 hours, maximum brightness on an iPad per the upstream span) are what the limitation Ograniczenia#2 (Duża ekspozycja laboratoryjna) silently relies on.

findings.fix_direction: Drop losowanym and the 4-hour and five-evening details unless a stored passage supports them, or state explicitly that they come from the upstream summary and were not confirmed in the abstract that was checked.

findings.text: Spróbuj zakończyć korzystanie z jasnego ekranu wcześniej
findings.why: The study compared reading the same material on a light-emitting device versus a printed book. That is a substitution of medium, not an earlier cut-off of screen use. Ending screen use earlier (a timing change, covering any screen activity) was not manipulated. The only stored support for the timing advice is NHS guidance (devices right before bed; relax at least 1 hour before bed), which the item does not tie to any sentence. The item does not call the extension an editorial example or say that the timing was not tested, although Ocena redakcyjna partly hedges it.

evidence.text: Here we compare the biological effects of reading an electronic book on a light-emitting device (LE-eBook) with reading a printed book
do not watch television or use devices, like smartphones, right before going to bed, because the blue light makes you more awake
睡前一小时不看发光屏幕，要看就看纸书或不开屏幕灯的墨水屏

findings.fix_direction: Say that the study tested the medium (light-emitting device versus paper) and not the cut-off time, and mark the earlier-cut-off advice as editorial or guidance-based, naming NHS as the basis for it.

findings.text: ogranicz jasne ekrany, jeśli utrudniają ci wyciszenie
findings.why: Two scope shifts. (1) The sources speak of light-emitting devices, not bright ones. The exposure was an iPad at maximum brightness, and brightness as a dose was not tested, so jasne can suggest that dimming is enough. (2) The trigger jeśli utrudniają ci wyciszenie is added by the adaptation. The measured outcomes are physiological (melatonin, circadian timing, morning alertness) and may not be noticed by the reader, so a reader who does not feel disturbed gets no advice although the same outcomes were found in all participants as a group.

evidence.text: Participants reading an LE-eBook took longer to fall asleep and had reduced evening sleepiness

findings.fix_direction: Use a wording faithful to light-emitting screens (not only bright ones), note that brightness settings were not tested, and justify or remove the subjective trigger, since the outcomes are not limited to felt difficulty winding down.

findings.text: Nie badano każdego telefonu, trybu nocnego ani ekranu z tuszem elektronicznym.

findings.fix_direction: Say that the stored source describes a single light-emitting e-book device and that phones, night mode and e-ink were not covered, rather than implying partial phone testing.

findings.why: The upstream fallback was paper or an e-ink reader with the screen light off. The item keeps only paper as a concrete example and mentions e-ink only as not tested. A reader who reads on an unlit e-ink device gets no statement that this is the case the original treated as equivalent to paper (an inference, correctly removed as untested), and no statement that a backlit e-ink device does emit light. Because the item allows any spokojne zajęcie, a path still exists, so this does not change what a reader would do materially.

findings.text: Nie traktuj jednej godziny jako naukowo ustalonej granicy dla wszystkich urządzeń.
findings.why: The item never introduces a one-hour rule, so a reader alone with this text cannot tell what is being denied. The one-hour figure comes from the upstream title, and the cited NHS page says to relax at least 1 hour before bed. A reader who opens NHS may see an apparent contradiction. Whether a one-hour cut-off is or is not scientifically established cannot be decided from the stored texts (one abstract and one NHS page), so the negative claim is only partly supported.

evidence.text: 睡前一小时不看发光屏幕，要看就看纸书或不开屏幕灯的墨水屏

findings.fix_direction: Say in the same sentence that popular advice and NHS guidance mention about an hour, and that this study did not test any cut-off time; avoid the unqualified naukowo ustalonej.
